coverageSpotVerification.detail: The coverage manifest maps every suite-required assertion in every attempted milestone (M1 7/7, M2 22/22, M3 7/7, M4 5/5, M5 6/6, M6 5/5, M8 6/6) with no gaps. Nineteen mappings were read against the mapped test source and, where useful, re-executed. Every sampled mapping exercises the assertion's observable: m1-a11 goes as far as asserting img.complete && naturalWidth>0; m6-a13 re-derives every entity from the action log and checks 8 classes of field; m8-a01 derives the six expected totals from a different query path than metrics:insights and then reads them off the rendered screen; m3-a15 replays all three installed seed segments twice and diffs history ids and chat count. Three mappings are weak but not dishonest, and are recorded rather than penalised: m2-a24 (no-duplicates/no-gaps is checked over one social:list call plus a rendered-count comparison, not across the paginated pages the client uses - the grader verified the paged walk independently); m3-a11 (the jump is asserted only as isVisible(), which does not establish scrolling - the grader measured the scroll movement independently); m4-a07 (clears with emoji:"none" rather than re-tapping the same emoji, though the UI maps that gesture to the same call). No mapping was found that claims an assertion the mapped test does not touch.

defects.summary: social:trending hard-errors at the scale envelope whenever no post falls in the trailing 24 h. The query scans the posts table through the likes index and post-filters on _creationTime, so an empty window makes take(10) walk all 50,228 posts and the request dies with "Your request timed out performing too many system operations" after ~15 s. Trending is unusable at the envelope, and the failure is deterministic rather than load-dependent.
defects.evidence: trace.md#o5-grader-probes; grading/evidence/o5-followup.json - 5/5 consecutive attempts on the scale instance failed at 15.0 s; newest scale post age 31.4 h; the same query returns 10 ranked posts on the dev instance, where recent posts exist. Source: convex/social.ts trending (withIndex("likes").order("desc").filter(...).take(10)). The lane's own recorded probe (artifacts/m8-probes-full.json, p95 1.79 ms) was taken while the replayed corpus was still inside its own 24 h window, which masked this.

defects.summary: Following-feed reads degrade to multi-second latency and then hard failure at the scale envelope for accounts with small follow sets. social:list({tab:"following"}) post-filters the whole feed table for the viewer's actors, so the sparser the follow set the more of the 48k-row table is scanned. The app's own paging query social:page has the same shape, so the Following tab in the real client takes tens of seconds per screen at the envelope.
defects.evidence: trace.md#o5-grader-probes; grading/evidence/o5-followup.json - cold social:list({tab:"following"}): u0005 (5 follows) 10.5 s at limit 20 and "too many system operations" at limit 50 and 100; u0901 (the brief's named celebrity-follower) 7.3 s at limit 20, 14.5 s at limit 50, error at limit 100; u0500 (500 follows) 321 ms / 295 ms / 580 ms at the same limits. social:page six pages: 44.0 s for u0005 and 26.2 s for u0901. Warm repeats return in 1-5 ms from the Convex query cache, which is why the k=20-after-3-warm-ups p95s all read ~1.8-2.5 ms. Source: convex/social.ts list/page.

defects.summary: The M8 acceptance test utc-seven-days-including-zero-render asserts that the six days before today carry no activity, so re-running the documented acceptance entrypoint on any day after the data was created fails and aborts the rest of the M8 suite. The produced coverage file then reports m8-a03, m8-a04, m8-a05, m8-a06 and m8-a07 as missing and the milestone suite as failed, even though all five behaviours are correct.
defects.evidence: trace.md#p1-suite; grading/evidence/acceptance-all.log and grading/evidence/grader-run-suite-m8.json - assert(after.days.slice(0,6).every(d=>d.posts===0&&d.likesReceived===0)) fails because the fixture posts were created on 2026-09-05 and the grader ran on 2026-09-06. scripts/acceptance-m8.mjs. All five assertions pass under independent grader verification (grading/evidence/m8-insights.json).

defects.summary: The M2 acceptance test scroll-pagination-both-tabs drives pagination with five page.mouse.wheel events separated by 250 ms waits and then asserts the rendered count reached the server count. On a loaded host the wheel events do not move the React Native Web ScrollView, so the test fails and reports m2-a22, m2-a23 and m2-a24 as missing even though pagination works.
defects.evidence: trace.md#m2-pagination; grading/evidence/m2-pagination.json - the same tab paginates 20 -> 103 immediately when the scroll container's scrollTop is set directly; 31 wheel-driven iterations produced no growth on the Following tab in the same session in which the Global tab grew 20 -> 122. Host load average 19-30 during the run (grading/evidence/uptime-*.txt). scripts/acceptance-m2.mjs.

defects.summary: The profile-feed branch of social:list applies .take(limit) before filtering out replies and accepts no `before` cursor, so a profile whose recent activity includes replies silently returns fewer than `limit` top-level posts with no way to page further. The M8 insights test relies on this call to derive expected totals, so its expected values would also drift once an author exceeds the limit.
defects.evidence: trace.md#defects - convex/social.ts list: `const posts = await ctx.db.query("posts").withIndex("author",...).order("desc").take(limit); return ... posts.filter(p=>!p.parent)`. Consumed by components/Social.tsx ProfileFeed with limit 200 and by scripts/acceptance-m8.mjs.

defects.summary: Ordinary chat and post media is served from unauthenticated bearer URLs (/api/storage/<uuid>), so a URL captured while the holder was authorised keeps serving after they lose access to the chat. This is the Convex storage model rather than lane code, and the two revocation paths the brief does test are unaffected: delete-for-everyone deletes the blob (404 afterwards) and view-once never issues a URL at all.
defects.evidence: trace.md#m5-a06 - grading/evidence/m5-a06-followup.log: an unauthenticated fetch of an ordinary media URL returns 200. Compare grading/evidence/m4-m5-api-phaseA.json (200 before delete, 404 after).

O1.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ("M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap") and the 90 anchor ("every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts"), nearer 90 on breadth and nearer 60 on completeness.
O1.justification: 100 of 119 in-scope atomic assertions pass under independent execution (M1 13/13, M2 27/27, M3 14/15, M4 12/12, M5 12/12, M6 6/13, M7 0/9, M8 16/18). That is well past the 60 anchor - M5, M6 (web) and M8 are as solid as M1-M4, not patchy. It falls clearly short of 90 on two counts the anchor names explicitly: M7 was never attempted (9 assertions not-run; artifacts/milestones.json status "not-run"), and the platform-proof artifacts for the offline claims do not exist (artifacts/simulator-m6.json and simulator-m8.json both record pass:null, so m6-a01..a07, m8-a17 and m8-a18 are undemonstrated). The one substantive web miss is m3-a02: DM bubbles render no sender avatar (0 of 100 in the DM view, 6 of 9 in a group), which the brief's M3 acceptance item 1 requires. Quality of what does pass is high: the two builder-suite failures in the grader re-run (m2 pagination, m8 day buckets) were both test brittleness, not product defects, and all five underlying behaviours verified pass independently.

O2.anchorsCited: Between the 30 anchor ("multiple high-severity defects in core flows") and the 60 anchor ("a few medium defects off the happy path"), placed below the midpoint because both major defects sit in core read paths rather than off the happy path.
O2.justification: Two major defects, both in core read paths and both only visible at the published scale envelope: social:trending hard-errors deterministically once no post falls in the trailing 24 h (d-01, 5/5 attempts), and Following-feed reads take 7-10 s cold and then error outright for small-follow-set accounts, including the brief's named celebrity-follower fixture (d-02, and 26-44 s for six pages through the client's own paging query). Three minor defects (d-03, d-04, d-05) and one cosmetic (d-06). Against that, the grader found no correctness defect at all at ordinary scale across a wide probe surface: 18 cross-user and unauthenticated authorization probes were all denied, removed-member delivery cut off correctly while pre-removal history was retained, message-key takeover and non-member sends were refused, idempotent set-state survived three retries of the same mutation id without toggling, and all eight spec bounds (2000-char message, 500-char post, 50-char group name, self-DM, self-follow, 5-image post, 7-char password) behaved correctly. The score is held down by the severity and the core-path location of d-01/d-02, and held up by the complete absence of ordinary-scale correctness defects.

O4.anchorsCited: Against the 60 anchor ("reads work; offline writes lost or mis-ordered, or receipts wrong after flush") and the 90 anchor ("reads, ordered queued writes, receipt transitions, and offline search all behave as specced on the native proof - on full runs including M8's durable-queue restart and multi-device convergence evidence"), with the dimension's "honesty of any gap between claim and guarantee" clause applied.
O4.justification: Scored from the harness choreography artifacts. The 60 anchor's failure modes are all absent: artifacts/choreo-m6.jsonl offline-message-queue-flush-in-order shows two offline sends exposing a "pending" receipt, flushing in send order on the recipient and both walking to "read" (flushMs 105.8); artifacts/choreo-m8.jsonl shows dual-device warm-offline convergence in server-arrival order, exactly once, on all three clients, with both receipts reaching read; artifacts/choreo-m5.jsonl shows warm-offline search over synced messages and disappearing-expiry purge across a relaunch. But two of the 90 anchor's four clauses have no evidence on any carrier: cold-start offline (reads, cached media, offline search, and the view-once non-render) and M8's durable-queue restart. artifacts/simulator-m6.json and simulator-m8.json both record pass:null with explicit reasons, and no web substitute is possible - the grader confirmed a cold web start with connectivity cut fails at navigation, as expected for a non-PWA carrier. The honesty of the gap is exemplary and is what keeps this at 55 rather than lower: the simulator artifacts, the README ("Native simulator launch artifacts are not qualifying offline-flow proofs") and run-record.json all state plainly that the native offline proof was not obtained, and nothing in the lane claims otherwise.

O5.bandRationale: First-match over the frozen order 0, 30, 60, 90, 75. Band 0 does not fire: the grader re-verified invariant-manifest conformance directly against the running replay instance and every named O5 fixture is exact (u0500 following 500 and 100 conversations, u0005 following 5, u0900 followers 900 and posts 200, u0901 following 5, g0001 50 members and exactly 10,000 messages counted by full paging), the replayed corpus counts match all 18 perEntityCounts fields of invariant-manifest-combined.json, the replayed scale.log SHA-256 matches the frozen fixture digest, all 167,157 actions settled across all 13 verb classes, and no replay wall cap was exhausted (884 s execution; the instrument's cap table is still a P3 placeholder). Band 30 fires on both of its clauses. A probe errors at the envelope: the grader's Trending probe failed 5 out of 5 times with "Your request timed out performing too many system operations" after 15 s (defect d-01), against the frozen envelope rule "No probe may time out, error, or OOM at the envelope". And a degradation rule fails: the Trending mid-curve clause, computed by the lane's own faithful implementation of the frozen predicate (values[1] <= values[0] + (values[2]-values[0])*4/9), is false at 1.9089 ms against a 1.7876 ms line (artifacts/scale-safety-probes.json). That second clause is a 0.12 ms margin at ~1.8 ms and is within measurement noise, so the band rests mainly on the probe error. Bands 60 and 90 are unreachable regardless: the instrument's absolute p95 ceilings and replay wall cap were never calibrated out of their P3 placeholders, so no ceiling utilisation can be established at all and the 90 branch's "<=50% of ceiling" condition cannot be met. Grader-measured rules that do pass, warm, at the final checkpoint: following 500-vs-5 ratio 1.40, deep-page 50-vs-1 ratio 1.04, celebrity read path 1.12, cold-sync of the 100-conversation probe user completed at 2.83 ms p95.
